newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai firms helped by interest rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai firms helped by interest rate cuts.

text.p: China's two bank interest rate cuts this year have helped Shanghai firms obtain more loans from banks and deposit more money in their bank accounts, the Shanghai Securities News said on Monday.

In the first nine months, Shanghai banks lent out 30.5 billion yuan more in loans than in the same period last year, with most of the money going to state-run companies, the newspaper said. It did not give absolute figures.
Of the increased lending, 80 percent was short-term loans, indicating an improvement in the financing of some Shanghai firms, the newspaper said.
By the end of September, company deposits in Shanghai banks rose by 22.3 billion yuan, or 36.5 percent, compared with the end of last year, it said, but gave no absolute figures.
